# Process

The running process: its command-line arguments, environment, identifier and exit.

## Installation

Add `Process` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
Process = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/Process` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Allocator`](/docs/api/allocator) 0.1.0
- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0
- [`FreeBSD`](/docs/api/freebsd) 0.1.0 (FreeBSD only)
- [`Io`](/docs/api/io) 0.1.0
- [`Linux`](/docs/api/linux) 0.1.0 (Linux only)
- [`macOS`](/docs/api/macos) 0.1.0 (macOS only)
- [`Memory`](/docs/api/memory) 0.1.0
- [`Path`](/docs/api/path) 0.1.0
- [`Thread`](/docs/api/thread) 0.1.0
- [`Windows`](/docs/api/windows) 0.1.0 (Windows only)

## Guide

The running process — its command-line arguments, environment, identifier and exit — and the child processes it starts.

### What it provides

| Module                                                     | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`Arguments`](/docs/api/process/arguments#arguments)       | [`ArgumentCount`](/docs/api/process/arguments#argument-count), `Argument`, and [`Arguments`](/docs/api/process/arguments#arguments) for walking them in order                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`Environment`](/docs/api/process/environment#environment) | [`Variable`](/docs/api/process/environment#variable) for one value by name, [`Environment`](/docs/api/process/environment#environment) for walking every [`EnvironmentVariable`](/docs/api/process/environment#environment-variable), and `SetVariable` and `RemoveVariable`                                                                                         |
| [`Exit`](/docs/api/process/exit#exit)                      | [`Exit`](/docs/api/process/exit#exit), which ends the process with a status, and [`CurrentId`](/docs/api/process/exit#current-id)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Executable`                                               | [`CurrentExecutable`](/docs/api/process/executable#current-executable), the path of the file the process is running, as the system loaded it                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`Command`](/docs/api/process/command#command)             | [`Command`](/docs/api/process/command#command), which describes a program to start, and [`Stdio`](/docs/api/process/command#stdio) for its standard streams                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`Child`](/docs/api/process/child#child)                   | [`Child`](/docs/api/process/child#child) with [`Wait`](/docs/api/process/child#wait), [`TryWait`](/docs/api/process/child#try-wait) and [`Kill`](/docs/api/process/child#kill), its [`ExitStatus`](/docs/api/process/child#exit-status), and the [`PipeReader`](/docs/api/process/child#pipe-reader) and [`PipeWriter`](/docs/api/process/child#pipe-writer) streams |
| [`Capture`](/docs/api/process/command#capture)             | [`Command::Capture`](/docs/api/process/command#capture), which runs a program and keeps its output, error and status                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

The module names describe where each declaration comes from; they are not part of an import path.

### Example

```rux
import Path::OsStringView;
import Process::{ ArgumentCount, Arguments, Variable };

func CountFlags() -> uint {
    var flags: uint = 0;
    var walk = Arguments();
    for argument in walk.Skip(1) {
        let units = argument.Units();
        if units.length > 0 && units[0] as uint32 == 0x2D {
            flags = flags + 1;
        }
    }
    return flags;
}

func HasHome() -> bool {
    let home = Variable("HOME") ?? OsStringView();
    return !home.IsEmpty() && ArgumentCount() > 0;
}
```

```rux
import Allocator::SystemAllocator;
import Io::IoError;
import Process::Command;

func Version() -> bool ! IoError {
    var command = Command(SystemAllocator(), "git");
    command.Argument("--version");
    let captured = command.Capture(SystemAllocator())?;
    return captured.Status().Success() && captured.Output().length > 0;
}
```

### Design

Arguments and environment values are native text, `Path::OsStringView`: bytes on the Unix systems and UTF-16 code units on Windows, exactly as the system handed them over. Nothing obliges either to be valid UTF-8 or UTF-16, so a program that needs text converts with `ToText` and decides what an unconvertible argument means. The first argument is the program as it was invoked, a name or a path the parent chose.

Every view of an argument or variable borrows storage the process owns for its whole life, so reading them allocates nothing and a view can be kept anywhere. Linux and FreeBSD keep the vectors on the stack the kernel built, which the entry stub records for `Core::ProcessStartFrame`; macOS has dyld record them in libSystem; Windows hands over one command line, which is split once with `CommandLineToArgvW` so that the arguments are the ones the C runtime would give, and one environment block, which is read once. The first read happens on first use and is kept, so a program that starts threads should read what it needs before it does.

Names are matched the way each system matches them: exactly on the Unix systems and without regard to ASCII case on Windows. `SetVariable` and `RemoveVariable` keep their changes in a table beside the environment the process started with, which [`Variable`](/docs/api/process/environment#variable), [`Environment`](/docs/api/process/environment#environment) and every child this package starts consult first. Their text is never freed, so every view handed out stays valid. Windows is told of each change as well; the C library's own environment on the Unix systems is not, so code outside Rux that reads it there does not see the change.

A [`Command`](/docs/api/process/command#command) collects a program, its arguments, a working directory, environment changes for the child, and what each standard stream is connected to: this process's own, nothing, or a new pipe. A part the system cannot take, such as text with a NUL in it, is remembered and reported when the command is started, so the parts can be given without checking each. On Linux, FreeBSD and macOS the child is started with the C library's `posix_spawnp`, which finds the program through `PATH` and reports a program that could not be started as `NotFound` or the system's reason rather than as a child that exits; a program that starts children is therefore linked against the C library. On Windows it is started with `CreateProcessW`, from a command line quoted the way the C runtime splits one, so each argument arrives exactly as it was given. On the Unix systems a relative program path is looked up after the child has changed to its working directory; on Windows, before.

A [`Child`](/docs/api/process/child#child)'s pipes are `Io` streams the caller takes and owns; closing the writer ends the child's input. [`Wait`](/docs/api/process/child#wait) closes that writer first, so a child that reads to the end is not left waiting. [`Capture`](/docs/api/process/command#capture) reads standard error on a second thread while it reads standard output, so a child that fills one pipe while the other is being read never deadlocks. A child that is dropped without waiting keeps running; on the Unix systems its status then stays with the system until this process ends.

[`Exit`](/docs/api/process/exit#exit) ends every thread at once and reports its status to the parent, which sees the low eight bits on the Unix systems and all thirty-two on Windows. Nothing is flushed or destroyed on the way out, so returning from `Main` remains the ordinary way to finish.

### Types

| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`ArgumentIterator`](/docs/api/process/arguments#argument-iterator)         | A walk over the process's arguments in order, the program first.                                                                 |
| [`CapturedOutput`](/docs/api/process/capture#captured-output)               | What a program wrote to its standard output and error, and how it finished.                                                      |
| [`ExitStatus`](/docs/api/process/child#exit-status)                         | How a child process finished.                                                                                                    |
| [`PipeWriter`](/docs/api/process/child#pipe-writer)                         | The writing end of a pipe into a child's standard input.                                                                         |
| [`PipeReader`](/docs/api/process/child#pipe-reader)                         | The reading end of a pipe from a child's standard output or error.                                                               |
| [`Child`](/docs/api/process/child#child)                                    | A child process this one started.                                                                                                |
| [`Stdio`](/docs/api/process/command#stdio)                                  | What a child's standard stream is connected to.                                                                                  |

| [`EnvironmentIterator`](/docs/api/process/environment#environment-iterator) | A walk over the environment variables: those the process started with, in the order the system holds them, then those set since. |

### Functions

| Name                                                                   | Summary                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`ArgumentCount`](/docs/api/process/arguments#argument-count)          | How many arguments the process was started with, the program itself included.                              |
| [`Argument`](/docs/api/process/arguments#argument)                     | The argument at `index`, counting the program as argument zero, or none past the last one.                 |
| [`Arguments`](/docs/api/process/arguments#arguments)                   | Every argument the process was started with, the program first.                                            |
| [`Environment`](/docs/api/process/environment#environment)             | Every environment variable of the process.                                                                 |
| [`Variable`](/docs/api/process/environment#variable)                   | The value of the environment variable `name`, or none when it is not set.                                  |
| [`SetVariable`](/docs/api/process/environment#set-variable)            | Sets the environment variable `name` to `value`, for this process and every process it starts from now on. |
| [`RemoveVariable`](/docs/api/process/environment#remove-variable)      | Removes the environment variable `name`, for this process and every process it starts from now on.         |
| [`CurrentExecutable`](/docs/api/process/executable#current-executable) | The path of the executable file the process is running, as the system loaded it.                           |
| [`Exit`](/docs/api/process/exit#exit)                                  | Ends the whole process at once, reporting `code` to its parent.                                            |
| [`CurrentId`](/docs/api/process/exit#current-id)                       | The identifier the system gave this process.                                                               |
